idea.en: Join both cavae into one plane through the atrium.

note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Superior vena cava

steps.en: What you see: Both venae cavae drain into the right atrium in one line with the thin interatrial septum between them. The fossa ovalis flap may flicker at the mid septum.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values: Cava 21 mm or less with collapse above 50 percent means right atrial pressure near 3 mmHg.
Cava above 21 mm with collapse below 50 percent means right atrial pressure near 15 mmHg.
Bubbles crossing to the left heart within three beats of right atrial opacification mean an intracardiac shunt.
Pitfalls: A Eustachian valve can direct cava flow at the septum and fake a shunt without colour confirmation. Valsalva timing decides a bubble study; release exactly as the atrium fills.

analogy.en: Landmarks to confirm: Superior vena cava

spot.en: Landmarks to confirm: Superior vena cava

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Coronary sinus mistaken for the inferior vena cava. Correct it by following the vessel, since the sinus runs in the groove and never lines up with the superior cava.
Foramen ovale flap mimicking an atrial septal defect. Correct it by confirming any gap in two planes with colour before reporting a defect.
Too anterior a plane that loses the superior vena cava. Correct it by angling posteriorly until both cavae meet the atrium together.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at subxiphoid, sagittal right of midline, tilted to join both cavae.
Point the probe marker toward the head, about twelve o clock.
From the cava long axis, tilt to bring the superior cava into the same line without losing the inferior one. Small rocking finds the plane where the septum is thinnest and brightest.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Guide bubble contrast for shunt detection.

q.en: What must line up in the bicaval view?

o.en: Superior and inferior cavae with the septum

why.en: Both cavae meet the atrium with the interatrial septum between them.

q.en: Bubbles cross within two beats of atrial filling. What does this mean?

why.en: Crossing within three beats marks an intracardiac shunt such as a foramen ovale.

q.en: A flap flickers at the mid septum without colour flow. What is this?

o.en: Foramen ovale flap, a normal finding

why.en: A mobile flap without a colour gap is the normal foramen ovale flap.

q.en: What decides a bubble study most?

o.en: Valsalva timing with release as the atrium fills

why.en: A well timed release raises right atrial pressure exactly when bubbles arrive.
